Values: Pass % / mean judge score / input tokens per question / USD per Pass (Table 3). Temperature 0; 900 s and 80-step limits. The benchmark sets a per-answer Pass threshold (score >= 70), but the authors state no success criterion for a configuration as a whole, so no verdicts are given.

fields.why: The draft set its own verdict rule (Pass rate >= 70% works, 50-70 partly) by applying the per-answer Pass threshold to the configuration's Pass rate, and judged cost relative to the other configurations; both break the 2026-11-23 rule (verdict only from an author-stated criterion, each configuration on its own). Metric values checked against Table 3: all correct

fields.v: SWE-QA benchmark as published (15 repos x 48 questions). 2 architectures x 4 models (Gemini 2.5 Flash, Gemini 2.5 Pro, Gemini 3 Flash, Qwen3-235B), paired within model. Held constant: repositories, questions, models, judge, rubric, framework (LangChain), temperature 0, step and time limits; tool sets differ by design (constitutive of the paradigms). Acceptance: LLM judge against reference answers. Repetitions: 1 run per question per condition. Human intervention: none. Not compute-matched

Semantic better on accuracy for every model: Pass diff +5.6 (2.5 Flash), +10.0 (2.5 Pro), +49.6 (3 Flash), +10.6 (Qwen) pp; score diff +6.7 to +30.9; Cliff's delta 0.14-0.76; all McNemar and Wilcoxon significant after FDR. Semantic cheaper in tokens and dollars for every model (Deep ~2.3x cost per correct answer). Deep led on 1 of 15 repos (django +3.0). 41.8% of Deep failures were planner-sub-agent coordination breakdowns, 91% of them silent

Yes: distinguished paradigms consistently (threshold sweep 50-90 and repository-level bootstrap keep the ordering). Single run per condition. Limitations stated: one harness per paradigm; tool space and orchestration co-vary; no harness sensitivity analysis; LLM judge; single benchmark, Python only, possible contamination; not compute-matched; latency environment-dependent

Results limited to single-question read-only QA over indexable repositories; long multi-task sessions (context hygiene), non-indexable or volatile repositories, and code-editing tasks not studied; future: compute-matched baseline, other languages and contamination-controlled benchmark, hybrid router

No replication package or data link given (only the Deep Agents library repository). No pre-registration. Language: Python. Values from Table 3 (p. 15), Table 4 (p. 16) and Table 5 (p. 28; columns jumbled by pdftotext, percentages from text p. 26-29). Minor inconsistency: 2,878 Deep runs reported (p. 23) against 4 x 720 = 2,880 questions per architecture; not explained. Study cost reported: $1,591.49 in total (Table 6, p. 37). Study not about SDD; relevant to context engineering in coding agents (sub-agent delegation used by Claude Code, Codex)
